notes: SR5 a and b are right on every probe. On c, 'a SAME clause (see page VII-19)' means the file-area SAME AREA clause, and the text settles it when read with its neighbours. SAME RECORD AREA is a format of the Sort-Merge chapter's own clause, and SR5 a names it expressly when it means it; the pointer away from that clause to the Sequential I-O clause designates the one form Sort-Merge's clause lacks, SAME AREA. GR2c of the same clause writes 'a SAME AREA or SAME RECORD AREA clause' when it means both. VII.2.13's own matching rule (SR3c) is written for 'a SAME AREA clause'. The rule exists because a SAME AREA clause shares 'all storage areas assigned to the files' (VII.2.13.4 GR1), which a sort may borrow (XI.2.5.4 GR2b). And 2002 restates c for the file-area format (§2002:12.3.6.2 SR10) with no 2002 change entry for SAME beyond FILE-CONTROL placement. CCVS-85 ST135A (SAME RECORD AREA USELESS-FILE DEADWEIGHT-FILE with SAME SORT SORTFILE-2E USELESS-FILE) agrees, though it is a net, not the authority. The compiler applies c to every file-area clause (COBOL2738) and not to SAME RECORD AREA, which is what c says.

next.reason: 1985 (a) and (b) are kept: §2023:12.4.6.4.3 SR6 and SR7 allow a file in one record-area SAME clause and a sort or merge file in one sort-merge-area clause, and §2023:12.4.6.2 '{ same-clause }...' allows several. (c) changed: 1985 covers a non-sort file that 'appears in a SAME clause (see page VII-19) and one or more SAME SORT AREA or SAME SORT-MERGE AREA clauses'; the VII-19 SAME clause is 'SAME [ RECORD ] AREA FOR file-name-1' (§1985:VII.2.13.2), so it includes SAME RECORD AREA. §2023:12.4.6.4.3 SR10 limits it to a file 'specified in a file-area format SAME clause and in one or more sort-merge-area format SAME clauses'. SAME RECORD AREA FOR F1 F2 with SAME SORT AREA FOR S1 F1 is refused by 1985 (c) and accepted by 2023 (SR7).
